teams.heading: Fiji drop to bottom of the table after losing to Scotland
teams.body: Fiji sit bottom of the table after suffering three consecutive defeats in their current campaign. The team has scored 49 points across those three matches. They have also conceded 145 points during the same period, leaving them with a point difference of minus 96. This run follows a 17-33 loss to Scotland in their last fixture. It contrasts with 2023, when the side reached a peak of No. 7 in the world rankings.

teams.heading: England Women's rugby team draw with Canada finishing historic unbeaten run
teams.body: The Red Roses’ remarkable sequence of 39 successive Test victories has come to a close following a 26-26 draw against Canada at Sandy Park. Despite England leading late into the final quarter, they were unable to secure the win after a Canadian ruck turnover denied a potential match-winning score. John Mitchell reflected on the result, stating: “We were applying huge pressure, but we just didn’t convert. One Test match isn’t going to take us away from our purpose.”

lead.why: The end of a 39-match winning streak for the Red Roses is a historic development in English rugby.

teams.heading: France Women defeat Australia in dramatic comeback after stadium fire delay
teams.body: France Women secured a 29-26 victory over Australia in a chaotic Test match in Aix-en-Provence on Saturday. The hosts overcame a 19-point deficit and a mid-match delay caused by a burning bus outside the Stade Maurice David. Despite being reduced to 11 players during a turbulent first half, France rallied with 17 unanswered points in the final 25 minutes to complete the win. Coach Tim Walsh noted the Wallaroos were disappointed to let the match slip after the momentum shift.

teams.heading: Ireland Women succumb to USA comeback in WXV Global Series opener
teams.body: The Ireland Women’s rugby team suffered a frustrating 40-36 defeat against the USA in their WXV Global Series opener. Despite holding a 19-point lead following tries from Vicky Elmes Kinlan, Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald, Aoife Wafer, and Erin King, the hosts were overhauled in the second half. Head coach Scott Bemand admitted it was "a game we should have won," citing a loss of discipline and technical errors as the primary factors that allowed the USA to gain momentum.

teams.heading: Italy Women secure emphatic victory over Japan in competition opening match
teams.body: The Italy Women’s Rugby Team opened their WXV Global Series campaign with a dominant 55-21 win against Japan at Stadio Omero Tognon. The Azzurre established an early lead through Aura Muzzo and Alessandra Frangipani, before a second-half score from captain Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi helped secure their highest-ever points tally against the Sakura XV. Despite a challenging start under new coach Toshizumi Kitagawa, Japan struggled to contain Italy's attack as the hosts maintained their momentum throughout the opening fixture.

teams.heading: Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan named as Gloucester’s new leadership duo
teams.body: Wales hooker Dewi Lake has been appointed captain of Gloucester for the upcoming season, with fellow international Jac Morgan confirmed as one of his vice-captains. The pair, who joined the club from Ospreys, were chosen following a selection process involving input from the entire playing group. Gloucester head coach George Skivington noted that it was "important for us to wait" before confirming the leadership team, citing Lake’s experience as a factor in his appointment to lead the side moving forward.

teams.heading: Argentina's Men and Women Secure Gold at South American Games
teams.body: Argentina’s national sevens teams enjoyed a dominant campaign at the South American Games in Rosario, with both the men’s and women’s sides claiming gold medals. The men’s team secured their title with a 17–7 victory over Chile, while Las Yaguaretés completed an undefeated tournament by defeating Colombia 35–5. These results ensure both squads have successfully qualified for the 2027 Pan American Games, maintaining Argentina’s position as a leading force in regional rugby sevens.

teams.heading: Springboks make 13 changes as André Esterhuizen captains side against Australia
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has opted for significant rotation, naming 13 changes to the Springboks starting XV for the Perth Test. Centre André Esterhuizen will captain the side in Siya Kolisi’s absence, partnering Canan Moodie in midfield. Only lock Eben Etzebeth and winger Ethan Hooker remain from the team that faced New Zealand. Despite the wholesale changes, the visitors have reverted to a traditional 5-3 bench split, with Erasmus aiming to balance the development of his depth with the physical demands of the match.

teams.heading: Japan Brave Blossoms claim Pacific Nations Cup title after beating Fiji
teams.body: Japan’s men secured their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 after a 20-15 victory over Fiji at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium. The result, which elevated the team into the world’s top 10 rankings, was driven by a determined defensive effort and a decisive second-half try from Ben Gunter. Captain Naoto Saito hailed the breakthrough, stating, “It’s a great breakthrough to create history for Japan. It gives this young team great confidence. This is going to be the trigger for us.”

lead.why: Japan securing the Pacific Nations Cup title is the most significant recent development for the men's national side.

teams.heading: New Zealand Rugby considers bombshell proposal to exit Super Rugby Pacific
teams.body: New Zealand Rugby faces a pivotal moment this week, with stakeholders set to debate the future of the domestic game at a summit in Wellington. According to a report, a proposal to withdraw from Super Rugby Pacific has been tabled as a potential option. This would involve replacing the current competition and the NPC with a new 8-10 team national structure. While alternative options include expanding Super Rugby, the governing body is under pressure to address significant long-term financial sustainability concerns.

lead.why: The potential end of Super Rugby Pacific represents the most significant structural threat to the New Zealand game currently under discussion.

teams.heading: André Esterhuizen named Springboks captain as Rassie Erasmus rotates the squad
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has appointed André Esterhuizen as the 68th Springbok captain, leading a much-changed starting XV against Australia this weekend. With 13 alterations from the side that defeated the All Blacks, only lock Eben Etzebeth and winger Ethan Hooker retain their spots. Erasmus described the 32-year-old as the "right man" for the role, citing his versatility and leadership. The coach warned that the team may take time to find their rhythm after a period of limited match minutes.
